SELECTED_INDEX: 8  
CONFIDENCE: 0.25  
EXPLANATION: The dominant bands at 2973, 2931 and 2879 cm⁻¹ (plus the 1454 cm⁻¹ deformation) are typical C–H-stretch/-bend features of a fully saturated hydrocarbon framework (rule GFQ-003).  No band is seen in the 1650–1800 cm⁻¹ (C=O) or 3200–3600 cm⁻¹ (free O–H or N–H) regions, arguing against the alcohol-, peroxide-, sulfone- or amine-containing candidates (1–7, 9, 10).  Intense bands at 923, 894–876, 763, 623 and 577 cm⁻¹ are characteristic ring-breathing and deformation modes of rigid bicyclic/bridgehead systems such as 2-oxabicyclo frameworks (compare the known Raman pattern of 1,8-cineole / 2-oxabicyclo[2.2.2]octane derivatives).  Candidate 8 (SMILES C1C2CC13CC1OCC213) is the only option that is a saturated bicyclic ether with a single bridgehead oxygen and no additional heteroatoms that would introduce strong diagnostic bands (e.g., S–O, O–O, N–H) predicted by rules GFQ-025, GFQ-026, GFQ-069, etc., yet absent experimentally.  Therefore it best matches the observed purely hydrocarbon-like spectrum with ether C–O stretches at 1138 and 1036 cm⁻¹.
